column3: Legend of the Callejón del Muerto
column5: An Archbishop, on his way home from Basilica Santa Maria was the first to see the ghost of Don Tristan. Having failed in life to fulfill a vow to walk barefoot to the Blessed Virgin's shrine after she saved his son from illness; Don Tristan made the journey immediately after death.

column3: Francisco and Antonio - los Parados
column5: In the Calle de los Parados, two devoted lovers, Don Francisco Puerto y Solis and Señor Don Antonio Miguel del Cardonal, continue to futilely wait on street corners for Doña María Ysabel, even after her untimely death from a pestilence. Unaware of her passing, they steadfastly maintained their vigil in life and death, becoming part of the legend that still shadows the street today.

column3: Youthful Prince O'Donoghue the Prophet
column5: Prince O’Donoghue, famed for wisdom and eternal youth, vanished during a feast at Ross Castle by walking out across the lake and sinking beneath its waters. Each May Day he is said to reappear on a white horse with a radiant retinue, a vision believed to foretell a plentiful harvest.

column3: The Ghostly Bishop of Fingest
column5: Bishop Burghersh of Fingest, known for his tyrannical behavior and land theft during his lifetime, is said to haunt the village of Fingest, seeking to return the stolen land for peace in death. The ghostly bishop roams the fields, pleading for the land to be restored to its rightful owners, as the villagers and subsequent landholders continue to ignore his restless spirit.

column3: The Ghost of Bisham Abbey
column5: The ghost of Lady Hobby haunts Bisham Abbey, unable to find peace after having beaten her son, Hobby, to death centuries ago for not keeping his schoolwork neat. Her spirit is a curious site, appearing with reversed colors and constantly trying to wash her hands in a basin she can never reach, symbolizing her eternal guilt.

column3: The Bottled Terror of Kinlet Church
column5: Following his death, the wrathful spirit of Sir George Blount terrorized the village of Kinlet on a black horse until local clergymen successfully captured and sealed his ghost inside a glass bottle near his tomb.

column3: The Ghost of Dame Creswyke at the Manor House Hotel
column5: In the historic market town of Moreton-in-Marsh, the 16th-century Manor House Hotel is said to be haunted by the spirit of Dame Creswyke, who was murdered within the building in the late 17th century.

column3: The Grey Lady of Owlpen Manor
column5: Following her historic stay on the eve of the Battle of Tewkesbury in 1471, the spirit of Queen Margaret of Anjou is said to haunt the upper rooms of Owlpen Manor as a benevolent grey lady. Decades later, evacuee children sleeping in the house reported being visited by this exact noble lady in medieval attire whom they had never met.

column3: The Ghostly Rider of Hill Barn Farm
column5: A 19th-century farm labourer was repeatedly pursued by the apparition of his former master along a Cotswold track before meeting the spirit at midnight to receive a secret message concerning hidden money.

column3: The Phantom Horsewoman of Stoke Park
column5: Seventeen-year-old Lady Elizabeth Somerset, who tragically died after falling from her horse in 1760, is said to haunt the grounds of Stoke Park and the Dower House. Visitors and conservation workers frequently report hearing the phantom sound of galloping hooves echoing through the estate's woodlands where no horses have ridden for decades.

column3: The Specter of Claude Harvey at the Jerome Grand Hotel
column5: A former hospital maintenance worker whose mysterious death was ruled an accident is said to still haunt the elevator shaft and basement of the historic Jerome Grand Hotel.

column3: Julia Lowell of the Copper Queen Hotel
column5: Guests staying in Room 315 of Bisbee's historic Copper Queen Hotel frequently report feeling the phantom presence and whispered pranks of a former resident known as Julia Lowell.

column3: The Resident Handyman of Hotel Congress
column5: A long-term resident handyman who lived at Tucson's Hotel Congress for over three decades reportedly continues to play practical jokes from beyond the grave.

column3: The Spirits of the Hornibrook Mansion
column5: Constructed in Little Rock in 1888, the historic Queen Anne Victorian mansion—now operating as a bed and breakfast—is said to be haunted by its original builder, who died tragically shortly after its completion.

column3: The Phantom of the Tampa Theatre
column5: A historic 1920s movie palace in downtown Tampa is said to be haunted by the ghost of a long-time projectionist who died after working in the booth and a mysterious apparition that occupies Seat 308.

column3: The Spectral Guest of the Moana Surfrider
column5: Following her tragic and unsolved poisoning in 1905, the co-founder of Stanford University, Jane Stanford, is said to haunt her former room and hallways at the Moana Surfrider Hotel in Waikiki.

column3: The Royal Phantoms of ‘Iolani Palace
column5: As the only royal palace in the United States, downtown Honolulu's ‘Iolani Palace is haunted by phantom intruders, guards firing at invisible soldiers, and the spectral forms of King Kamehameha III and his headless ancestor.

column3: The Ghostly Guardian of the Eldridge Hotel
column5: Room 506 of the historic Eldridge Hotel in Lawrence is said to be haunted by Colonel Shalor Eldridge, whose spirit manifests through unexplained cold spots, self-opening doors, and breath marks on mirrors.

column3: The Nanny of Park Avenue
column5: In Old Louisville, the shadowy specter of a former live-in nanny named Annie Whipple is said to haunt the curved staircase of a historic mansion after her tragic dabbling in spiritualism cost her her life.

column3: The Phantom of the Electric Chair
column5: Following her historic 1942 execution in the courthouse basement, the restless spirit of Toni Jo Henry is said to haunt the halls with inexplicable cold spots, flickering lights, and phantom noises. As Louisiana's only executed female inmate, her lingering presence remains a fixture of local lore.

column3: The Spirits of Battle Alley
column5: The historic Holly Hotel in Michigan is reputed to be haunted by several permanent spectral residents, including its original innkeeper and a playful young girl.

column3: The Spectral Guests of the Palmer House Hotel
column5: Built on the ashes of a burned hotel in Sauk Centre, this historic inn is famously haunted by a boy bouncing a ball, a tall man standing over beds, and even the spirit of local Nobel laureate Sinclair Lewis.

column3: The Haunting of the Captain Bailey House
column5: Visitors to this historic seven-gabled home in Brownville report that doors refuse to stay shut due to the lingering presence of a Civil War captain and his wife.

column3: The Phantoms of the Proprietary House
column5: Visitors on haunted history tours of the colonial Proprietary House in Perth Amboy encounter the restless specters of Revolutionary War figures and former residents.

column3: The Ghost of Room 18 at the St. James Hotel
column5: Built in 1872 by former presidential chef Henri Lambert, the St. James Hotel in Cimarron witnessed dozens of murders during the Wild West era, and its locked Room 18 is said to be haunted by a card player who was murdered after winning the hotel in a poker game.

column3: The Spectral Mistress of the Staab House
column5: The historic Staab Mansion at La Posada Hotel in Santa Fe is said to be haunted by Julia Staab, who fell into a profound depression following the death of her newborn child and lived as a recluse until her death in 1896.

column3: The Ghostly Echoes of Edgar Allan Poe at the Providence Athenæum
column5: The historic Providence Athenæum library on Benefit Street preserves the lingering memory and reported ghostly presence of Edgar Allan Poe following his ill-fated romance and dramatic breakup there.

column3: The Ghost of Sheriff Seth Bullock
column5: Guests and staff at a historic Deadwood hotel frequently report eerie encounters with its original builder and first sheriff, who still oversees the property from beyond the grave.

column3: The Grey Lady of Historic Tuckahoe
column5: A woman forced into an unhappy marriage after being separated from her true love haunts the boxwood path of her historic childhood home.

column3: The Spirit of Virginia Croxton at the Essex Inn
column5: An elderly resident who lived eighty years in a 19th-century mansion continues to share a guest room with overnight visitors long after her death.

column3: The Restless Founder of the Pfister Hotel
column5: A historic luxury hotel in downtown Milwaukee is widely reported to be haunted by its founder, regularly startling visiting professional baseball players with unexplained electrical and physical disturbances.

column3: The Haunting of Prince House
column5: Situated within Heritage Park, the historic Prince House is said to be haunted by the spirits of lumber baron Peter A. Prince's multiple wives who passed away during his lifetime.

column3: The Haunting of the Johnston House
column5: Built in 1911 by Dr. Robert James Johnston Sr.—who tragically died in the home in 1936—this historic house on Third Avenue East is frequently visited by the spirits of Dr. Bob and his young daughter Marjorie.

column3: The Specter of Fairacres Mansion
column5: The historic Fairacres Mansion in Deer Lake Park is said to be haunted by its former mistress, Grace Ceperley, and other restless spirits from its turbulent past.

column3: The Benevolent Fire Chief of the Old Fire Hall
column5: The historic castle-like fire station on Nicol Street is said to be haunted by Nanaimo's first fire chief, who died of pneumonia after battling a harsh winter blaze in 1937.

column3: The Rolling Cannonballs of the Nanaimo Bastion
column5: Nanaimo's iconic coastal landmark is reportedly haunted by former caretakers and phantom noises, most notably heavy cannonballs rolling across the wooden floorboards.

column3: The Haunting of Canada's Oldest Operating Movie Theatre
column5: Operating continuously since 1913, the Patricia Theatre in Powell River's Townsite is haunted by a strict former dentist and active poltergeist phenomena.

column3: The Haunting of the Carlin House (The Trickle Inn)
column5: The historic Carlin House along the Trans-Canada Highway is said to be haunted by a family grandmother and other lingering paranormal energies.

column3: The Hanging Judge of Bastion Square
column5: The historic courthouse in Bastion Square is said to be haunted by Sir Matthew Baillie Begbie, whose slender figure glides down the main staircase.

column3: The Ghost of Caretaker Arthur Sharpe at the Washington Avenue Grill
column5: Built as a 1913 lumber mill, the historic Washington Avenue Grill is said to be haunted by a missing 1930s caretaker and the spirits of two tragic lovers.

column3: The Phantom Firefighter of the Capitol Theatre
column5: The historic Capitol Theatre on Main Street is haunted by the ghost of a volunteer firefighter who was crushed to death during a 1924 blaze.

column3: Walter Golding's Haunting at the Imperial Theatre
column5: The historic Imperial Theatre in Saint John is said to be haunted by its former passionate manager, Walter Golding, who still watches over the lobby and lounge named after him.

column3: The Ferryland Lighthouse Visitor
column5: In the early 1970s, an artist and his family living in an isolated lighthouse dwelling on the Avalon Peninsula received a late-night visit from a mysterious old man who later turned out to be a constable who had died twenty years prior.

column3: The Ghost of Kitty Casey
column5: Following her tragic death in 1862 while her husband was imprisoned, the spirit of Kitty Casey has long been rumored to roam the foggy shores and drokes of Sandy Cove.

column3: The Haunting of Blinkbonnie
column5: Built over 170 years ago by town co-founder Charles MacDonald, the historic Blinkbonnie estate is said to be haunted by its former patriarch and lingering family spirits.

column3: The Haunting of the Bell Mansion
column5: The historic Bell Mansion in Sudbury is said to be haunted by its original resident, Katherine Bell, whose ghostly footsteps and rustling skirts still echo through the halls.

column3: The Tragedy and Ghosts of Cedar Street
column5: The former Castonguay family home—now operating as the HourGlass Restaurant—is reportedly haunted by the couple who were tragically murdered there in 1957.

column3: The Phantom of Sunnyside Manor
column5: The historic Heintzman House in Thornhill-Markham is said to be haunted by figures from its 19th-century past, including a former coachman and the property's original owner, Colonel George Cruickshank.

column3: The Ghost of Captain Colin Swayze
column5: The resident ghost of a Canadian militia officer killed during the War of 1812 haunts a historic inn in Niagara-on-the-Lake as long as the British flag flies overhead.

column3: The Slain War Bride of Room 207
column5: A British war bride waiting for her soldier husband during the War of 1812 was tragically killed by an American soldier, and her spirit is said to haunt Room 207 of a historic hotel.

column3: The Spirits of the Nicholas Street Gaol
column5: The historic 19th-century Carleton County Gaol, now operating as a hostel, is said to be haunted by the restless spirits of former inmates, most notably Patrick J. Whelan, who was publicly hanged there in 1869.

column3: The Phantom of the Château Laurier
column5: Ottawa’s iconic luxury hotel is said to be haunted by its original visionary, Charles Melville Hays, who perished on the RMS Titanic just weeks before the hotel opened.

column3: The Phantom of Nancy Montgomery on Yonge Street
column5: Drivers along Yonge Street have long reported seeing a translucent female apparition darting in front of their vehicles near the 1843 historic murder site of housekeeper Nancy Montgomery.

column3: Richard Bridgland (The screaming man)
column5: Richard Bridgland was smothered by a wall of clay at the brickworks.

column3: Mary Ann Bennett (The Lady of Rose Court (private))
column5: Mary Ann Bennett died from an overdose of opium.

column3: Sarah Sharp (The Watercress Lady) at Pinnock Bridge
column5: An elderly watercress seller—later identified as Sarah Sharp—accidentally set her clothes alight near a bridge and was found burned to death by the roadside in 1911. Local lore claims that on the anniversary of her death her ghost reappears, wrapped in flames and screaming for help.

column3: The hanging Schoolmaster
column5: Actually a papermaker Henry Edgar Martin who died in the same way ascribed to the schoolmaster - ‘strangulation by hanging by a halter from a tree’.

column3: Kittie Rankie at Abergeldie Castle
column5: French Kate (Catherine “Kittie” Rankie), a serving woman condemned as a witch and executed on Craig-na-Ban—still haunts Abergeldie Castle, where she was once held in the cellars. Sightings of her ghost have been reported in the dungeon and the clock tower.

column3: Elizabeth Holles - The Old Hell-Cat of Raby
column5: The feud at Raby Castle began when Lady Elizabeth Holles—wealthy, headstrong, and opposed to her son Gilbert’s choice of bride—led the furious destruction of much of his inheritance, forcing the family into the courts to halt the ruin. Local legend maintains that Elizabeth never calmed, and that the “Old Hell-Cat” still haunts the castle battlements, pacing and knitting with red-hot needles.

column3: The Green Lady (Donna Leonora Oviedo)
column5: Sir John Bolle fell in love with a Spanish heiress he was bound to protect, but refused to marry her because he already had a wife, and she withdrew to a convent and died of heartbreak. Her ghost—known as the Green Lady—was then said to appear around Thorpe Hall, where the Bolle family kept a place set for her at meals

column3: Rosamund Guy - the Irby Boggle
column5: A betrothed couple vanished after a meeting in the woods, and legend holds that Neville Randall murdered Rosamund Guy and fled. Her bones were later said to be found beneath a tree marked with their initials, and her ghost was reputed to haunt the wood for centuries

column3: Thomas de Gretham at Thornton Abbey
column5: A fourteenth-century abbot named Thomas de Gretham was said to have been discovered bricked up in a dungeon alcove, seated before a book with pen in hand, having been left to die for practicing witchcraft. His ghost was then reportedly seen around Thornton Abbey, especially near the gatehouse

column3: The Murderous Tom Otter
column5: Tom Otter secretly married Mary Kirkham while already having a wife and child, then murdered her and was swiftly tried, hanged, and displayed in a gibbet near the crime scene. Macabre rumours, apparitions, and exaggerations soon grew around the murder, turning the case into local legend and giving the lane and nearby sites his name

column3: George Nelson Ghost at Cadeby Hall
column5: Cadeby Hall’s roadside memorial marks the spot where sixteen-year-old George Nelson died in 1885, and local lore claims his ghost still rides out on the anniversary of his death, spooking travellers along Barton Street. Over time the Hall gained further legends of curses, spectral huntsmen, and ghostly apparitions, turning a real family tragedy into a cluster of haunting tales

column3: Sidney Conway at Providence House
column5: The ghost of a small boy is said to haunt Providence House in Barton-upon-Humber, most active around Hallowe’en—heard running, crying, and playing tricks with doors, lights, and book-stands. The haunting is linked to a real child, Sidney Conway, who lived there when the building was an orphanage in the 1920s and died after falling into an overheated bath
